title: PFRDA Grade A 2026 — Pension Landscape PS17

content.prompt: Two subscribers have ₹24 lakh each at ordinary retirement: one under the NPS All Citizen Model and one under the government-sector NPS. Ignoring other choices or special circumstances, what are their respective maximum lump-sum portions under the current exit rules?

options.text: Both may take ₹19.2 lakh.
Non-government ₹19.2 lakh; government-sector ₹14.4 lakh.
Non-government ₹14.4 lakh; government-sector ₹19.2 lakh.
Non-government ₹24 lakh; government-sector ₹14.4 lakh.
Both may take ₹14.4 lakh.

sections.title: PFRDA Grade A 2026 — Pension Landscape PS17

explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:01:r1: For a large corpus at normal exit under the current rules, a non-government subscriber may ordinarily take up to 80% as lump sum (₹19.2 lakh of ₹24 lakh), while a government-sector subscriber may ordinarily take up to 60% (₹14.4 lakh), subject to applicable conditions.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:02:r1: Under the current All Citizen exit framework, completion of the prescribed 15-year subscription route can permit normal exit before age 60, subject to the applicable conditions.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:03:r1: For the applicable ₹8–12 lakh band, the current exit framework provides a special route allowing up to ₹6 lakh upfront and the balance through systematic unit redemption for at least six years, subject to the regulation.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:04:r1: At normal government-sector exit, the small-corpus rule permits full lump-sum withdrawal where the accumulated pension wealth is within the prescribed threshold; ₹7.8 lakh falls within that band.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:05:r1: Ordinary premature exit generally requires at least 80% of the corpus for annuity. 80% of ₹9 lakh = ₹7.2 lakh.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:06:r1: Death is governed by a separate exit treatment; the nominee/legal heir can receive the entire accumulated wealth, with other approved payout options also available under the applicable framework.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:07:r1: The current rule ordinarily requires a three-year interval between partial withdrawals, subject to the applicable conditions.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:08:r1: Ordinary Tier II is a voluntary, relatively liquid account. It ordinarily permits withdrawal while Tier I remains active; it is distinct from Tier I exit/annuity restrictions.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:09:r1: The Tier II Tax Saver variant is a special arrangement for eligible Central Government NPS subscribers and carries a three-year lock-in, unlike ordinary Tier II liquidity.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:10:r1: Under the 2026 NPS Vatsalya guidelines, up to two partial withdrawals are permitted before age 18 and up to two additional withdrawals between 18 and 21 after the prescribed fresh identity verification and subject to other conditions.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:11:r1: For the applicable Vatsalya exit after majority, a corpus below ₹8 lakh may be withdrawn fully, subject to the prescribed conditions.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:12:r1: If no choice is exercised by age 21, the current Vatsalya guidelines prescribe transition to the specified higher-equity Multiple Scheme Framework variant of the same pension fund rather than an automatic cash payout.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:13:r1: On death of the minor subscriber, the accumulated wealth is payable to the appropriate guardian/nominee/legal heir, with the applicable option to transfer to an eligible NPS account.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:14:r1: The post-1 October 2022 restriction applies to opening a new APY account by a person who is or has been an income-tax payer; it does not automatically cancel a qualifying earlier account.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:15:r1: Under APY, the spouse receives the same guaranteed minimum pension after the subscriber's death; after both subscriber and spouse die, the nominee receives the prescribed pension wealth. The 60% family-payout rule belongs to UPS, not APY.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:16:r1: Full assured payout benchmark = 50% of ₹80,000 = ₹40,000 for 25 years (300 months). Proportionate payout = ₹40,000×180/300 = ₹24,000.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:17:r1: The lower corpus is ₹20 lakh; 60% is ₹12 lakh. A final withdrawal reduces the assured payout proportionately under the UPS framework.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:18:r1: For the stated qualifying voluntary-retirement case, the UPS assured periodic payout begins from the date of notional normal superannuation, while specified lump-sum/final-withdrawal benefits may be available at voluntary retirement.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:19:r1: The applicable NPS-Lite/Swavalamban small-corpus schedule permits full lump-sum withdrawal at normal exit where accumulated pension wealth does not exceed the specified ₹2 lakh threshold.
explanations.pfrda:ps17:q:20:r1: Sukanya Samriddhi uses a balance-based education-withdrawal rule (up to 50% of the preceding financial year-end balance under the stated age/Class 10 condition). NPS Vatsalya uses a distinct contribution-based partial-withdrawal rule, currently up to 25% of contributions excluding returns for permitted purposes and subject to conditions.
